chapter_theme: One song at Tribhuvanam (திரிபுவனம்): the poet caught in the net of union that he enjoys even in dreams asks for Murugan's small red lotus feet; the praise names Murugan who taught his father the one thing and is lord of the siddhas of the shrine.

862.reading: The poet describes the women whose brows sweat and eyes sink as they speak sweet love and embrace, the lips' moisture sweeter than sugar, and says his life is caught and perishing in the net of a union he enjoys even in dreams; a man without fate or wit, he asks whether he will not gain the small red lotus feet that bring release. The praise names Devayanai, daughter of the thunderbolt-bearer, the sea crying out and the demons turning tail before the lion-like hero, Murugan who offered the one thing that gives experience to his father and received his worship, lord of the siddhas of Tribhuvanam who remain even when all the world perishes.
862.nuance: கனவிலும் நுகர்தரு கலவி: the union is enjoyed even in dreams, desire outlasting waking. அனுபவம் அளிதரும் ஒரு பொருள் அப்பர்க்கு அப்படி ஒப்பித்து அர்ச்சனை கொண்ட நாதா: the teaching of Siva again, here as 'the one thing that gives experience', after which the father worships the son.
